title: Jeremiah 23:9–15
context: Jeremiah begins a collection of sayings “concerning the prophets” with his own anguish (23:9), and the LORD indicts the land’s unfaithfulness and the profane prophets and priests of Samaria and Jerusalem, who strengthen evildoers so that no one turns from wickedness (23:10–15). Warnings about false prophecy are shared ground between the traditions.

verses.text: Concerning the prophets: My heart within me is broken. All my bones shake. I am like a drunken man, and like a man whom wine has overcome, because of the LORD, and because of his holy words.
verses.arminianNotes: Jeremiah speaks: “Concerning the prophets: My heart within me is broken.” Arminian readers see the prophet’s grief, as one shaken by the LORD’s holy words and by the corruption of other prophets.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see a prophet overwhelmed by the holiness of God’s word. Readers in this tradition note that a faithful messenger is not detached from his message but feels its weight.

verses.text: “For the land is full of adulterers; for because of the curse the land mourns. The pastures of the wilderness have dried up. Their course is evil, and their might is not right;
verses.arminianNotes: “For the land is full of adulterers; for because of the curse the land mourns.” Arminian readers see the people’s unfaithfulness bringing covenant curse on the land itself.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the land mourning under covenant judgment. Adultery here may include both literal sin and spiritual unfaithfulness, and readers in this tradition hold both senses as possible.

verses.text: for both prophet and priest are profane. Yes, in my house I have found their wickedness,” says the LORD.
verses.arminianNotes: “… for both prophet and priest are profane. Yes, in my house I have found their wickedness,” says the LORD. Arminian readers see corruption reaching even the temple and its leaders.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the LORD exposing sin among those set apart for holy service. Readers in this tradition take it as a sober warning that religious office does not guarantee faithfulness.

verses.text: Therefore their way will be to them as slippery places in the darkness. They will be driven on, and fall therein; for I will bring evil on them, even the year of their visitation,” says the LORD.
verses.arminianNotes: “Therefore their way will be to them as slippery places in the darkness.” Arminian readers see the consequences of chosen wickedness pictured as a treacherous path in the dark.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see judgment pictured as stumbling in darkness. The LORD’s word that he will bring evil on them is the language of just judgment, not of moral evil in God.

verses.text: “I have seen folly in the prophets of Samaria. They prophesied by Baal, and caused my people Israel to err.
verses.arminianNotes: “I have seen folly in the prophets of Samaria. They prophesied by Baal, and caused my people Israel to err.” Arminian readers see the northern kingdom’s false prophecy recalled as a warning.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see Samaria’s idolatry set beside Jerusalem’s sins. Readers in this tradition note that the northern kingdom’s fall had already shown where such prophecy leads.

verses.text: In the prophets of Jerusalem I have also seen a horrible thing: they commit adultery and walk in lies. They strengthen the hands of evildoers, so that no one returns from his wickedness. They have all become to me as Sodom, and its inhabitants as Gomorrah.”
verses.arminianNotes: “In the prophets of Jerusalem I have also seen a horrible thing.” Arminian readers see Jerusalem’s prophets judged even more severely, since they strengthen evildoers so that no one returns from wickedness.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the gravity of leaders who discourage repentance. The comparison with Sodom and Gomorrah shows how far Jerusalem has fallen, and readers in this tradition hear it as a sober indictment.

verses.text: Therefore the LORD of Armies says concerning the prophets: “Behold, I will feed them with wormwood, and make them drink poisoned water; for from the prophets of Jerusalem ungodliness has gone out into all the land.”
verses.arminianNotes: “Behold, I will feed them with wormwood, and make them drink poisoned water.” Arminian readers see bitter judgment matched to the bitter fruit of the false prophets’ influence.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see a fitting judgment for those who spread ungodliness through the land. Readers in this tradition note that the same imagery appears against the people in Jeremiah 9:15.
